368132.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner/Admin user, called {User-A} (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Everything below is at the same location, shown in the top bar next to the bell (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919").
  • The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • A desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • Two technicians at this location, called {Technician-A} (for example "Esther Howard"; use exactly this name) and {Technician-B} (for example "Jenny Wilson"; use exactly this name). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • A customer used by this case only, with one contact and one asset, so this case's work orders are kept apart from every other work order at the location. In this test it is called {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Empty Tech Column").
  • Two Approved work orders for {Customer-A}, called {Work-order-A} and {Work-order-B}, both led by {Technician-A}. Nothing for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-B}.
  • The work orders you will drag have no shift on the Schedule for their lead technician. Assigned to me is off.
368132.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type {Customer-A}'s name so only this test's work orders show.
  4. Make sure Assigned to me is off.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  6. Find {Technician-B}'s column.
  7. Look through the toolbar, the column header and any menus for a control to hide empty columns.
  8. Drag the {Work-order-B} card onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  9. Look at both column counts.
368132.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Step 6: {Technician-B}'s column is on the board even though she leads no work orders.
  • Step 7: There is no control anywhere to hide empty technician columns.
  • Steps 8 and 9: The card can be dropped on her column: {Technician-B} now shows 1 and {Technician-A} drops from 2 to 1.
  • Step 4: While Assigned to me is on or when nothing matches the filters, other rules apply (checked in other cases).
368132.moved: Setup block (7 steps) -> doc Part 1 steps 1-19 and Part 2; Needs/Build lines removed; [User-A]/[WO-1]/[WO-2] and named technicians/customer -> {User-A}/{Work-order-A}/{Work-order-B}/{Technician-A}/{Technician-B}/{Customer-A}.
368132.notes: Last expected line (a scope note, not a result) given the prefix Step 4 (the Assigned to me step) to meet the Step N shape; wording unchanged.

96956.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner/Admin user, called {User-A} (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). Everything below is at the same location, shown in the top bar next to the bell (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919").
  • The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • A desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • Three eligible technicians at this location, called {Technician-A} (for example "Esther Howard"), {Technician-B} (for example "Ralph Edwards") and {Technician-C} (for example "Dana Ortiz"); use exactly these names, the expected results name them. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Three staff members who must NOT be offered: an Office-role user {User-B} (for example "Owen Office"), a technician whose staff record is set to Inactive {Technician-D} (for example "Ivan Inactive"), and a technician enrolled only at another location {Technician-E} (for example "Lena Otherloc"); use exactly these names, the expected results name them.
  • A customer used by this case only, called {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Reassign List"), with one Approved work order {Work-order-A} led by {Technician-A}.
96956.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type {Customer-A}'s name in Search.
  3. Hover {Work-order-A}'s card in {Technician-A}'s column and click its More actions (…) button.
  4. Choose Reassign lead technician.
  5. Look at every choice listed in the dialog.
  6. Pick {Technician-B} and confirm the dialog with its confirm button (e.g. "Reassign").
  7. If a "Clear …'s scheduled shifts?" prompt opens, click Keep shifts.
  8. Open the same card's More actions menu again and choose Reassign lead technician.
  9. Pick Unassigned and confirm.
  10. If a "Clear …'s scheduled shifts?" prompt opens, click Keep shifts.
  11. Open the card's More actions menu again (it is now in the Unassigned column) and choose Reassign lead technician.
  12. Pick {Technician-C}, then click Cancel.
  13. Open the work order (click the card) and look at Lead Technician.
  14. Go back, pick Tech View in the display switcher and repeat steps 3 to 13 using the row's More actions button.
96956.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Steps 3, 4 and 14: The card's More actions menu (and the Tech View row's) offers Reassign lead technician, and choosing it opens the Reassign lead technician dialog.
  • Step 5: The dialog lists Unassigned and the eligible technicians of this location, e.g. {Technician-A}, {Technician-B} and {Technician-C}. {User-B}, {Technician-D} and {Technician-E} are not listed.
  • Steps 6 to 10: After picking {Technician-B} and confirming, the card is in {Technician-B}'s column (the row in his group), and the work order page shows Lead Technician {Technician-B}. After picking Unassigned and confirming, the card is in the Unassigned column and the work order has no lead technician.
  • Steps 12 and 13: After Cancel, nothing changes: the card stays in Unassigned and the work order still has no lead technician.
96956.moved: Setup block (7 steps) -> doc Part 1 steps 1-18 and Part 2; Needs/Build lines and the 'names stay as written' note removed (now 'use exactly these names'); [User-A]/[Tech-A..C]/[WO-1], Owen/Ivan/Lena and the customer -> {User-A}/{Technician-A..C}/{Work-order-A}/{User-B}/{Technician-D}/{Technician-E}/{Customer-A}.
96956.notes: Step 5 'Read every choice' reworded to 'Look at every choice' (observation only).

96958.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner/Admin user, called {User-A} (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). Everything below is at the same location, shown in the top bar next to the bell (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919").
  • The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • A desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • A second browser (or a private window) for signing in as the technicians.
  • Three eligible technicians at this location, called {Technician-A} (for example "Esther Howard"), {Technician-B} (for example "Ralph Edwards") and {Technician-C} (for example "Dana Ortiz"). Each of them can sign in (each staff record has an email and an accepted invite) and see their notifications. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • A customer used by this case only, called {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Notifications"), with one Approved work order {Work-order-A} led by {Technician-A}.
96958.custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-A}'s work order page and change Lead Technician from {Technician-A} to {Technician-B} there.
  2. In a second browser, sign in as {Technician-A} and write down any notification received for this change (notification bell, email, or none).
  3. In the second browser, sign in as {Technician-B} and write down any notification received for this change (notification bell, email, or none).
  4. In the first browser, open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  5. Type {Customer-A}'s name in Search.
  6. In the first browser, drag the card from {Technician-B}'s column into {Technician-C}'s column.
  7. If a "Clear …'s scheduled shifts?" prompt opens, click Keep shifts.
  8. In the second browser, sign in as {Technician-B} and write down any notification received.
  9. In the second browser, sign in as {Technician-C} and write down any notification received.
  10. Repeat steps 4 to 9 in Tech View with the row's More actions > Reassign lead technician, moving it back to {Technician-A}.
96958.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Steps 2 to 10: A lead change made in Board View or Tech View produces exactly the same notifications as a lead change made on the work order page (steps 2 and 3 compared with steps 8, 9 and 10). The product owner records that no notification is sent on a lead change today, so none is expected in either place.
